source_title: Harness Engineering: How to Build Software When Humans Steer and Agents Execute
speaker: Ryan Lopopolo (Member of Technical Staff, OpenAI)
verdict: VERY HIGH — compressed 18-min conference version of Lopopolo's harness engineering thesis; the 8 talking points (prompts-as-lint, QA plans, persona docs, durable failure-class solutions, anti-slop instruction, tests-as-invariants, parallel P3 workers, remove-from-loop) map 1:1 to concrete changes in our tmux orchestrator; keynote is arguably more actionable than the 75-min Latent Space podcast because every minute is a directly adoptable pattern
key_insight: Humans steer, agents execute: implementation is free, the scarce resources are human time, attention, and context window — encode every non-functional requirement in lint rules, tests, and prompts, then remove yourself from the loop

cross_reference.relationship: Same speaker, same core thesis, different venue and format. Podcast (April 7) is 75 min deep dive on Symphony/Elixir architecture and zero-code metrics. Keynote (April 9) is compressed 18-min with novel material: 'humans steer, agents execute' framing, anti-slop prompt, QA plan gray-box pattern, persona-oriented docs, prompts-everywhere enumeration, economic framing of code-is-free.

adoptable_patterns_for_orchestrator: Prompts-as-lint: rewrite lint error messages as fix instructions; wire reviewer agent to consume lint output as prompt body
QA plan gate: add QA_PLAN_CHECK phase between WAIT_FOR_PR and REVIEW-FIX LOOP; require media attachments as proof of work
Persona-oriented docs: split CLAUDE.md into CLAUDE-orchestrator.md / CLAUDE-worker-*.md / CLAUDE-reviewer.md
Durable failure-class solutions: when same pattern appears 3+ times in devlog, spawn harness-improvement agent
Anti-slop instruction: literally add 'Do not produce slop. Do not accept slop.' to orchestrator + worker system prompts
Structural invariant tests: files <350 lines, folder depth <4, exports per file <20
Parallel P3 spawn: fire 4 workers on isolated git worktrees for ambiguous/low-stakes issues, reviewer picks best
Human-interventions metric: track human_interventions_count in orchestrator-tmux-state.json as regression signal
key_quotes: Every one of you is a staff engineer. You have as many team members as you can possibly drive concurrently and have tokens to support.
Zod is type load-bearing infrastructure for our AI future.
The models crave tokens. We can operationalize our codebase to give them tokens.
Just go build things. Do not hesitate to remove yourselves from the loop.
You can simply say 'do not produce slop. Don't accept slop.' You won't get slop in your codebase.
If I wrote the code myself, I have strong feelings about how it runs. If I didn't, I don't.
I use cookbooks to generate skills to write prompts to write prompts.
talking_points_summary: Late-2025 convergence: GPT 5.2 isomorphism with senior engineers, code is free, 5-5000 engineer-equivalents per human
New scarce resources: human time/attention, model context window, systems thinking as primary skill
Code-is-cheap economics: P3s cleared in parallel, i18n from day one, migrations always finish, zero authorship attachment
Codebase legibility: structure native to agents, respect scarce context, make tokens predictable, persona-oriented docs
Encode non-functional requirements in writing: lint rules, docs, review agents, agents.md — 500 decisions per patch must be specified
Durable solutions to failure classes: lint-enforce retry/timeout wrapping on every fetch, then migrate entire codebase once
Prompts everywhere: agents.md, lint error messages, review agent PR comments, source-code-structure tests, cookbook-generated meta-prompts
Gray-box delegation via QA plans: reviewer asserts QA plan exists with media attachments; trust compounds, delegation scales
